source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Right prescriber identity, meaning the nurse verifies that the ordering clinician is physically present before each dose is given.","B":"Right insurance authorization, meaning coverage must be confirmed before any scheduled medication can be administered safely.","C":"Right documentation and right reason, which are commonly included in expanded medication-administration safety frameworks today.","D":"Right room number, meaning the client's assigned location is used as an additional identifier before medication administration."}}
source_row.rationale: Beyond the traditional five rights (patient, drug, dose, route, time), expanded frameworks commonly include additional rights such as right documentation (recording administration accurately) and right reason (understanding the rationale/indication for the medication), reflecting a more comprehensive approach to medication safety.
source_row.source_detail: AHRQ PSNet primer, Five Rights section: five rights alone do not ensure medication safety; expanded rights include documentation, action/reason, form, and response. Current AHRQ PSNet primer reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: ISMP — Expanded Rights of Medication Administration
source_row.stem: A nurse is reviewing the expanded "rights" of medication administration with a nursing student, beyond the traditional five. Which additional "right" is commonly included in expanded frameworks?
